newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs easier, Sakakibara ignored.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs easier, Sakakibara ignored.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures shed some of their recent gains on Thursday but remained largely unmoved by an eagerly-awaited speech by a senior Finance Ministry official.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau told reporters Japan's foreign exchange policy had not changed and the country welcomed developments in currency markets since April 1995.
The late afternoon comments, which provided a brief lift to the dollar, were largely shrugged off by the Japanese fixed interest market.
"He's just repeating the same thing," said a Japanese bank dealer. "There was some profit-taking early in the day which is a natural tendency after last night's spike up."
"The near-term market looks weak but the big picture is still very bullish," he added.
The lead June Euroyen contract was quoted at 99.18 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.20 after hitting a low of 99.16. Support is seen at 99.14/15.
December JGBs ended at 124.36 against their previous 124.53.
Eurodollar futures eased after the U.S. Federal Reserve's widely-anticipated decision to leave short-term rates unchanged on Wednesday.
"It was a highly expected move so there was no reaction," said the dealer.
Dealers said the market would scrutinise U.S. Consumer Price Index and retail sales data, due later on Thursday, for indications of consumer sentiment and confirmation of non-inflationary growth.
March Eurodollars ended one tick off an IMM close at 94.45.
